tools.name: Kimi K3

tools.description: Moonshot AI released the Kimi K3 weights on July 27, 2026, eleven days after the model itself launched. The 2.8T-parameter MoE ships in MXFP4 at roughly 594GB, with Kimi Delta Attention, Attention Residuals, 16-of-896 expert activation, native vision, and a 1M-token context window. Baseten, Fireworks, Together, OpenRouter, and SiliconFlow were serving it within a day, and vLLM and SGLang had day-zero support for self-hosting. Each host publishes its own model id for the same file, so routing config matters more than usual.

tools.name: Laguna S 2.1
tools.weeklyHighlight: 118B MoE built for agentic coding, 8B active per token, runs locally from one GGUF
tools.description: Poolside released Laguna S 2.1 on July 21, 2026 for agentic coding and long-horizon software engineering. The 118B-parameter MoE activates roughly 8B parameters per token across 256 routed experts, supports a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens, and can reason before and between tool calls. Poolside reports 70.2 percent on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 78.5 percent on SWE-bench Multilingual, and 59.4 percent on the public SWE-Bench Pro dataset, and published the evaluation trajectories behind those numbers. The official Q4_K_M GGUF runs locally through DwarfStar or llama.cpp.

tools.name: Robostral Navigate

Trained in simulation across roughly 2.4M trajectories and 350K scenes, it reached a reported 76.6% success rate on unseen R2R-CE environments and generalizes across wheeled, legged, and flying robots.
